headline: Highest risk is Devin’s broad workspace and write privileges colliding with Whisper’s unverified CLI-only audio pipeline; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by Whisper’s no-network, no-filesystem profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can ingest files, browser content, MCP outputs, and shared integrations, so attacker-controlled text could reach its instruction parser. Whisper has no filesystem, network, or MCP surface and is command-line only, so it is not a direct bridge back. The pair risk is therefore limited and mostly requires manual or integration-based handoff.
conditions: IF Devin is fed untrusted text from a repo, ticket, Slack thread, or MCP server, prompt injection is plausible.
IF Whisper output is copied into Devin without human review, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files into Devin.
Require human review before copying Whisper transcripts into Devin.
Strip instructions from audio transcripts before downstream use.
Restrict Devin MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources.
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores content outside expected fields.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, while Whisper only touches audio/speech and has no network egress or file read/write. There is no shared workspace or authenticated API path in the profiles, so leakage between them is not a default pathway. Any leak would require an external bridge such as manual export of transcripts.
conditions: IF audio transcripts are manually pasted into Devin, sensitive spoken content can enter its workspace.
IF Devin is given secrets in files or chat, those may be exposed in its outputs or integrations.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in audio that will be transcribed.
Redact transcripts before sending them to Devin.
Keep Devin workspaces separate from any audio-processing pipeline.
Limit Devin integrations to least-privilege scopes.
Review Devin outputs before sharing outside the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad write, git, shell, and network capabilities in a shared cloud workspace model, while Whisper is non-runnable and has no write or network capability. Direct write-write conflict is not shown, but Devin’s shared integrations and parallel sessions can still collide with external artifacts if Whisper transcripts are used as inputs or repo files are updated concurrently. Uncertainty about the orchestration layer pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Devin and another session modify the same repo or workspace path, git or file conflicts can occur.
IF Whisper-derived files are written into the same directory Devin edits, overwrite races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per session.
Use git branches with explicit merge review.
Lock shared files before Devin edits them.
Keep Whisper outputs read-only until promoted.
Pause parallel Devin sessions on the same repo.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can act autonomously inside its workspace and across integrations, so if it treats Whisper transcripts as authoritative, transcription errors can cascade into code changes, tickets, or messages. Whisper itself is only a speech model and does not verify downstream actions. The pathway exists, but the blast radius is bounded by human review and the lack of direct action authority in Whisper.
conditions: IF Devin consumes Whisper transcripts as source-of-truth without verification, transcription mistakes can propagate.
IF Devin is allowed to open tickets or commit code from transcript content, downstream errors become operational.
mitigations: Require verification against the original audio for critical transcripts.
Mark Whisper output as untrusted input in Devin prompts.
Add a review step before Devin commits or sends messages.
Use confidence thresholds to flag uncertain transcript segments.
Restrict Devin from auto-executing actions based on transcripts.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles code, chat, docs, and integration tokens in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while Whisper only touches audio/speech and has no requested secrets or network egress. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to accidental inclusion of sensitive spoken content in transcripts. The other agent is not cited because no separate compliance regime is shown for Whisper.
conditions: IF regulated content is spoken into Whisper and then stored or forwarded by Devin, compliance obligations may apply.
IF Devin workspaces are configured to retain transcripts longer than policy allows, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Do not speak regulated data into Whisper.
Set transcript retention to the minimum needed.
Store transcripts outside Devin unless required.
Review data-handling policy for audio-derived text.
Use redaction before any transcript export.
